summary: Linear search checks items one at a time. Binary search halves a sorted array on each step, so it needs far fewer comparisons on long arrays.
notes: Math.floor((low + high) / 2) rounds down. JavaScript's / always keeps the decimal, so 11 / 2 is 5.5.
low = mid + 1 and high = mid - 1 skip mid, because it was already checked.
Each search returns an object { index, comparisons }, and const { index, comparisons } = ... unpacks it. -1 means not found.
pitfall: Leaving out Math.floor gives no error. items[5.5] is undefined, so the search returns index -1 even for 88, which is in the array.
contrast: JavaScript has one number type and / always keeps the decimal, so it needs Math.floor where Python uses // and Java's int division rounds down by itself. A decimal index gives undefined instead of an error.
